item.title: Xi Visits Trump; Putin Consolidates Power; ICC Faces Sanctions: On Air, September 21, 2026
item.description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping will pay a state visit to the United States from September 23 to 25, meeting US President Donald Trump for talks. President Xi expressed hope on Monday that younger generations will advance Sino-US cooperation and foster mutual understanding, responding to students from 10 US universities who attended a youth exchange program in China. The leaders are expected to discuss issues including trade, artificial intelligence, and broader bilateral relations, even as Breitbart News refers to Xi Jinping as a "genocidal dictator."
President Vladimir Putin's United Russia party secured a record supermajority in the State Duma election, winning 355 of the 450 seats. Electoral chief Ella Pamfilova announced the preliminary results, which surpass the party's previous record of 343 seats.
Paramount settled a lawsuit with a coalition of 12 Democratic state attorneys general, clearing the path for its $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. The agreement binds Paramount to operate Warner Bros. Studios and Paramount Pictures separately, committing the combined company to release at least 30 films annually. A board will also be created to ensure the editorial independence of CNN, though advocates like the Committee for the First Amendment and Free Press expressed disappointment.
The Trump administration prepares sweeping sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC), measures that could cut the court off from much of the global financial system. Proposed sanctions would bar most transactions involving the ICC after a six-to-seven-month wind-down period, potentially preventing the court from transacting in US dollars or protecting witnesses. The United States objects to the ICC's arrest warrants for Israeli officials and past investigations into American military actions in Afghanistan.
President Donald Trump and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani will meet on Monday at Gracie Mansion, their third in-person encounter. The meeting occurs ahead of the United Nations General Assembly, where Trump is traveling to New York City this week.
The United States and Denmark reached a security deal concerning Greenland, which will develop a military presence on the territory and block Washington's adversaries from building bases. Shares of US-listed companies exposed to Greenland surged on Monday, with Greenland Energy soaring 159% and Greenland Mines up over 200%. Danish officials state the deal places Arctic security under NATO's responsibility.
President Donald Trump stated the Department of Justice and other US law enforcement agencies will rein in artificial intelligence risks "if they have to." Trump announced plans to create an "AI Force" and appoint an "AI czar," despite repeatedly calling potential dangers from AI a "hoax" in the past two weeks.
French President Emmanuel Macron and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced plans to deepen economic and defense ties following a meeting in Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon. The leaders discussed opportunities to share infrastructure in space and defense sectors, as well as cooperation in energy and telecommunications. Both leaders stated their countries are experiencing strained relations with the United States.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz vowed to keep his ruling coalition together after his Christian Democratic Unionist (CDU) party suffered defeats in two state elections. The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party won the most votes in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, where the CDU failed to reach the 5% threshold to enter the state parliament. This marks the CDU's worst result in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern since 1945.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.

item.title: North Korea Fires Missiles; Ukraine Strikes Moscow; Trump Bans Reporters: On Air, September 20, 2026
item.description:
North Korea launched two short-range ballistic missiles toward the sea on Sunday. The launches occurred from the Wonsan area, with the first missile flying 450 kilometers and the second traveling more than 600 kilometers. Both missiles landed in the North's eastern waters. South Korea's presidential office urged North Korea to halt ballistic missile launches, citing U.N. Security Council resolutions.
Ukraine launched its largest drone attack to date on Moscow and the surrounding region on September 20, 2026. The assault struck a major oil refinery and other targets. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin described the attack as the largest ever on the capital. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated defense forces used Flamingo, Palianytsia, and Pelican long-range weapons. The attack occurred on the final day of Russia's parliamentary elections.
The U.S. military struck a suspected drug smuggling vessel in the Caribbean Sea on Saturday, killing four people. U.S. Southern Command (Southcom) stated Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere executed a lethal, kinetic strike on a go-fast vessel. The vessel operated along established narco-trafficking routes. This strike marks the latest action in the Trump administration's operation against alleged Latin American traffickers.
Iran-backed Houthi rebels warned countries against joining Saudi Arabia in Yemen's revived civil war. Mohamed al-Bukhaiti, a Houthi political bureau member, stated his group assured the Trump administration it would not attack U.S. vessels in the Red Sea. Al-Bukhaiti confirmed the Houthis target only the Saudi enemy in the strait. US President Donald Trump confirmed his administration "had discussions" with the Houthis.
Police arrested Aleema Khan, the sister of Pakistan's jailed former prime minister Imran Khan, at her house in Lahore. A spokesperson from Imran Khan's political party, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), confirmed the arrest. Aleema Khan was detained under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance. She was taken to Kot Lakhpat jail and sent to jail for 30 days. The arrest occurred ahead of a planned PTI protest march on September 27.
Luxembourg's government deployed additional detection capabilities to strengthen airspace monitoring following drone sightings near Luxembourg airport. The airport temporarily suspended operations late on Friday, September 18, due to these unidentified drones. Luxembourgish Prime Minister Luc Frieden stated the country cooperates with NATO allies regarding the incident. Frieden also noted the country had been "confronted with something new."
President Donald Trump posted AI-generated images on Truth Social mocking the news organizations he banned from the White House. House Majority Leader Steve Scalise stated he does not know why Trump banned the three news outlets. Representative Maria Elvira Salazar defended Trump's move, citing his style. Senator John Barrasso stated Trump's decision to ban CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House does not violate the Constitution. Journalists from these three outlets were denied entry to the White House on Saturday morning.
The John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts closed indefinitely on Tuesday. This followed a federal judge's decision last week to deny President Trump's attempt to add his name to the building. Trump's allies on the center's board voted to close the facility, citing safety concerns. Trump, who chairs the center, claimed online that a security guard narrowly avoided death from falling plaster.
The U.S. Embassy issued a travel warning for Israel ahead of Yom Kippur. The warning advised Americans traveling to and from the country to prepare for potential flight cancellations.
Full bias analysis and source spectrum: https://news.voidvision.org/onair/.
